title: Polynomial power lifting for an inclusion gives a universal homeomorphism
statement: Let $f:R\to B$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative rings. For every integer $n\geq0$, let $f_n:R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ be the coefficientwise extension [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Suppose that for every $n$ and every $b\in B[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ there are an integer $N>0$ and $a\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ with $f_n(a)=b^N$. Then for every commutative $R$-algebra $C$, the homomorphism $C\to C\otimes_RB$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, induces a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_RB)\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ of Zariski topological spaces [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite-generation, characteristic or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Remark 3.2.2 (a ring map is universally adequate iff all its polynomial extensions are adequate) and Lemma 3.1.4 (an adequate inclusion of rings induces an integral homeomorphism on spectra), arXiv 1005.2398 pp.10-11, applied to the injective adequate map C/ker -> C (x)_R B, whose kernel ker(C -> C (x)_R B) is nilpotent because integral injective ring maps are surjective on spectra and surjectivity is stable under base change; this is the argument of Proposition 3.3.5 (2)=>(1) (printed pp.496, 498), without that proposition's finite-presentation and characteristic-zero local-isomorphism content. The single-map homeomorphism input is also Stacks algebra.tex Tag 0BR8 (lemma-powers). Primary published PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Take $n=0$ in the hypothesis: the polynomial rings with no variables are $R$ and $B$ by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so every $b\in B$ has a positive power in $f(R)$. Injectivity gives $\ker f=0$, whose elements are nilpotent. Thus [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism] applies to $f$ and gives a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, in particular a surjection.

source.place: Tag 0BR8, lemma-powers, homeomorphism clause, applied before base change

proof.text: Fix any commutative $R$-algebra $C$, and put $D=C\otimes_R B$ and $g:C\to D$, $g(c)=c\otimes1$. The commutative ring structure and the algebra inclusions are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The surjectivity just proved and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change], with $R\to R^{\prime}$ equal to $R\to C$, imply that $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ induced by $g$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 00FI, lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal, final base-change assertion; tensor product as in Section 00CV

proof.text: Let $z\in D$. By the generation assertion in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $z=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\otimes b_j$ (absorbing scalar coefficients into $c_j$). Put $P=\sum_{j=1}^m b_jt_j\in B[t_1,\ldots,t_m]$. The hypothesis gives $N>0$ and $A\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_m]$ with $f_m(A)=P^N$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], evaluate $B[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\to D$ using $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ and $t_j\mapsto c_j\otimes1$. The multiplication and balancing identities of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give $P\mapsto z$ and $f_m(A)\mapsto g(A(c_1,\ldots,c_m))$: both maps on $R$ are the common structural map and both send $t_j$ to $c_j\otimes1$. Therefore $z^N=g(A(c_1,\ldots,c_m))$. For the empty sum take $P=0$, $A=0$, $N=1$. Thus every element of $D$ has a positive power in $g(C)$.

source.place: Section 00CV, tensor-product generation and balancing; explicit polynomial evaluation argument written by Q07 (the expansion of Alper Remark 3.2.2)

proof.text: If $c\in\ker g$ and $\mathfrak p\subset C$ is any prime, the surjectivity in step 2 supplies a prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ with $g^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Since $g(c)=0$, we have $c\in\mathfrak p$. Apply the radical-intersection formula of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] to the zero ideal in $C$: membership in every prime means $c\in\sqrt{(0)}$, or $c^k=0$ for some $k\geq1$. Consequently every element of $\ker g$ is nilpotent. No uniform nilpotence exponent is asserted.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, radical as the intersection of the primes containing the ideal

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism] to the commutative ring map $g$, using the positive powers from step 3 and its elementwise nilpotent kernel from step 4. This gives precisely the required homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_R B)\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. Since $C$ was arbitrary, the conclusion holds for every indicated base change.

source.place: Tag 0BR8, lemma-powers, homeomorphism clause, applied after base change
